rv.q: For the right audience this is a near-perfect production, and the perfect outing for any child in your life: inner or actual.
By the end as they wave their hockey sticks aloft, you will be looking forward to next term and cheering the Malory Towers girls along.
The musical numbers are something of a mixed bag, however, with a slightly awkward juxtaposition between Ian Ross’ original compositions and some recognisable tunes of the era.

cn.t: Emma Rice's adaptation of Enid Blyton's beloved boarding school series receives a mixed reception, with critics finding it nostalgic but uneven in its appeal to both longtime fans and younger audiences.
